title: Should Homework Be Abolished?
text:
Many parents and teachers argue that homework helps students practise what they have learned in class. In my opinion, a moderate amount of homework is genuinely useful. It encourages independent study and builds discipline that students will need at university and at work. However, excessive homework can cause exhaustion and leave little time for sport, hobbies, and rest. Therefore, the real question is not whether homework should exist, but how much of it is reasonable.

Some researchers claim that long assignments have only a small effect on exam results for younger children. This evidence is worth considering, although it does not apply equally to every subject or age group. Schools could set shorter tasks, offer clear feedback, and avoid giving the same amount to every student. In conclusion, I believe that homework should be purposeful, balanced, and adapted to each learner's needs.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what does homework help students do?
options: Practise what they have learned in class

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what could schools do to improve homework?
options: Set shorter tasks and offer clear feedback
Give the same amount to every student

questions.text: What can be inferred about the writer's view of excessive homework?
options: It is an excellent way to build discipline
It can harm students' rest and wellbeing
It is needed for every student's success
It has no effect on students at all

questions.text: Why does the writer say the research evidence is worth considering but not decisive?
options: Because it applies equally to every subject and age group
Because it does not apply equally to every subject or age group
Because the researchers were not qualified
Because the evidence is about adult workers

paragraph_translations: Wielu rodziców i nauczycieli twierdzi, że zadania domowe pomagają uczniom ćwiczyć to, czego nauczyli się na lekcjach. Moim zdaniem umiarkowana ilość zadań domowych jest naprawdę przydatna. Zachęca do samodzielnej nauki i buduje dyscyplinę, której uczniowie będą potrzebować na studiach i w pracy. Jednak nadmiar zadań może prowadzić do wyczerpania i zostawiać mało czasu na sport, hobby i odpoczynek. Dlatego prawdziwe pytanie nie brzmi, czy zadania domowe powinny istnieć, lecz ile z nich jest rozsądne.

Niektórzy badacze twierdzą, że długie prace domowe mają niewielki wpływ na wyniki egzaminów u młodszych dzieci. Te dowody warto wziąć pod uwagę, choć nie dotyczą one w równym stopniu każdego przedmiotu ani grupy wiekowej. Szkoły mogłyby zlecać krótsze zadania, udzielać jasnej informacji zwrotnej i nie dawać wszystkim uczniom tej samej ilości pracy. Podsumowując, uważam, że zadania domowe powinny być celowe, zrównoważone i dostosowane do potrzeb każdego ucznia.
